resources.string: No reminders yet. Keep your chats safe.
What dcAI sees and when parents are told.
Sensitive image detection is off: no model for it is installed on this phone.
A friend you just met online is still a stranger. Keep your address and school to yourself.
If someone asks you to keep a secret from your parents, that is a sign to tell them.
A free gift that asks you to move to another app deserves suspicion.
A photo once sent is hard to take back. Think before you send.
You can stop replying to anyone who makes you uncomfortable.
Use a different password for every account.
Messages in chat apps that integrate dcAI are assessed for risky patterns, such as asking for photos, moving to another app, or keeping secrets from parents. You get a short reminder in the moment.
Names, phone numbers, addresses, schools and accounts are masked on the phone before anything is sent. Message text is not stored.
Masked messages, to be assessed. Only the pattern, level and advice for the parent are stored.
An image you are about to share is checked on the phone. Faces and personal data such as a student card or an address are blurred. Images in a risky chat are checked too, and their text is assessed.
Images always stay on this phone. If dcAI blurs by mistake, show your parent. They review it on this phone with the PIN.
Only a label, such as \"personal data blurred\". The image itself is never sent.
Holds risky sites on this phone.
Site names are matched against a list on the phone. Adult, gambling, scam, malware, dating, drug and hate sites are held, and you are told why.
The sites you open stay on this phone. App traffic does not pass through dcAI. The VPN key icon at the top of the screen shows this protection is on.
Only the category of a held site, such as \"gambling\". The site\'s name is not sent.
A voice note in a chat that is already risky is turned into text, masked, then assessed like any message. This comes to the app soon.
The recording goes to Meta\'s transcription service to become text. The text is masked before it is assessed.
When you send with the Check key, what you typed is assessed too, for example if you share personal data or need support.
Your typing is masked on the phone before it is sent. The keyboard only sees your own typing.
Masked text, each time you press Check.
A parent has not approved this protection on the dcAI dashboard, so dcAI does not use it.
Everything that is on for this phone. Switching a protection off needs the parent PIN.
If a protection is switched off, the parent is told on the dashboard.
Done by a parent from the dashboard
A parent disconnects this phone from the dcAI dashboard. dcAI then stops, and its data on this phone is deleted.
dcAI does not work in secret. The \"dcAI is on\" notification shows the whole time dcAI runs, and you can always open this page.
dcAI guides chats in apps that integrate dcAI and the text you type with the dcAI keyboard. Other apps are not read.
Personal data is masked on the phone. Images stay on the phone. For sites, only the category is sent.
Parents receive levels, patterns and conversation starters. They do not receive message text or images.
An AI assessment is an estimate and can be wrong. If you think dcAI got it wrong, tell your parent.
Site lists: UT1 Blacklists, Université Toulouse Capitole, CC BY-SA 4.0. The lists on this phone are hashed adaptations under the same license.
Face and text detection in images: Google ML Kit, on-device models.
Pattern assessment: Muse Spark and Llama by Meta.
Open source components: AndroidX, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin, OkHttp, kotlinx.serialization, under their own licenses.
dcAI blurred this image. A parent enters the PIN to see it and decide.
No parent PIN is set on this phone. The image stays blurred.
Does this image need to be blurred?
dcAI held a %1$s site. If you think that is wrong, show your parent.
dcAI held %1$s (category %2$s). A parent enters the PIN to allow it on this phone.
Daily limits, bedtime and short-video breaks.

A parent sets limits for time online per day and per category, bedtime, and a break after watching short video for a long time. You get a reminder before time runs out, and you can ask for more time with a short reason.
The list of apps and when you use them stay on this phone. dcAI sees only app names and how long, never what is inside.
Total minutes per category (video, games, social, other) per day, minutes during bedtime and the longest session. A request for more time is sent with its reason masked.
To count how long apps are used on this phone.
Reads message notifications in chat apps, so what the other person writes is assessed too.
For the break screen when time is up or at bedtime.
Turn on usage access so time can be counted.
Bedtime in %1$d minutes. Time to get ready.
%1$d minutes of watching. How about a short break?
%1$d minutes of time online left today.
Your parent has not allowed more time right now.

While the industry works on making technology ever smarter, our job is to make sure our children stay safe using it.
dcAI is one of the main pillars of digitalsafe.app, a startup dedicated to building an ecosystem for digital education, ethics and safety.
A digital safety and ethics platform for school-age children and their families.
An AI research assistant that puts academic integrity first, for students, researchers and academics.
An agentic AI LMS that helps teachers manage and run learning in a way that is ethical, accountable and transparent.
Safe and friendly mathematics games and learning that bring a real, interactive and measurable experience through Extended Reality (XR/VR) and Artificial Intelligence.
